I had a thought about what makes a puzzle enjoyable vs. a slog.  I think I've underestimated the value of making some wrong totally "virgin" entries ...like Force for FARAD tonight.

Oddly I think making errors in this initial stage can make for a much more exciting solve.

The whole area around the incorrect entry is poisoned in most or all of its squares.  This makes solving the crosses, and their crosses, impossible because of the wrong letter.  Sometimes in that situation I'll think of the right answer for that the cross, but rule it out because of that incorrect letter.

Then, in desperation, when finally the incorrect entry is reconsidered, *if* the right one comes to mind, then suddenly that entire area opens up.  You see a place for two or maybe three words when you've finally removed the incorrect letters.  

Then those new answers produce more crosses for them, and Bob's your uncle.

So now consider a puzzle when you can get a few entires, but they are all right.  But since nothing is coming easy, when it does come it doesn't really unlock anything else.  And you do this until it's done.  A slog.

I'm reminded of that computer game Minesweep.  Sometimes when a button was clicked and entire section of went away.

Correcting an error in a tough puzzle is kind of like that, I think.

I mostly wanted to let the group know that this is a really lovely space and you brighten many days in many ways you might be unaware of. Only a few months ago, on the cusp of middle age, I asked my husband of over a decade for divorce. While moving out of our house I broke some vertebrae in a car crash. In this new low point of my life, feeling frustrated and in pain of every kind, diving into the NYXWs has helped me so much—not just learning from each puzzle and all of your contributions, but flexing some too-long atrophied mental muscles of my own, and reconnecting with what remains of a younger, happier, more confident me. Even the most tedious pedantry in the comments brings me happily back pre-marriage days pursuing my PhD when it seemed like the world was my oyster.

The NYTXW archive is a TREASURETROVE, or a mine, of early human puzzling tools going back almost 300,000-299,960 years. Discoveries made there will make you reassess your “perception of the skills and sophistication of early people” as per the Schöningen effect and our columnist’s explanation of it. In those archives, an early analog of an unknown-to-me rap group like WRECKXNEFFECT might be some off-off-Broadway play from the 1920s. Zero chance I know it. But those early stone-wielding cruciverbalists (hi Barry :) didn’t have the convenience of simple crosses to allow them to discover new arcana. No, they had to deal with minor European rivers, moth-balled papal vestments, and random-vowel-laden seamstressery. Best case, you still had to append an ‘a-‘ or an ‘en-‘ to words that had only had that done to them once before in history: like “atip” or “ensile”.  

So, if completing this puzzle makes you think you are oh, so highly evolved, spear (sic.) a thought for our forebears, and remember that while you may be feeling like a TOTALSWEETHEART, compared to them and their puzzle chops, ITSNOTEVENCLOSE.
